_doc: Flow facts of the UCX-OS kernel (ARCH=riscv/hf-riscv-e) for rttools.wcet (format: rttools/wcet/annotations.py). The selectors name functions and calls, not addresses, so the file holds for any build of the kernel; an image whose jump tables cannot be read (objdump listing) adds the targets in a file of its own. Params: tcb = task control blocks on one PE (tasks of the PE plus the idle task), the length of the circular list that krnl_schedule, krnl_delay_update and enable_receiver walk; heap_blocks = blocks of the heap of one PE (allocations of app_main and of the driver plus the packets in flight), the length of the list that ucx_malloc walks; ddma_wait = passes of the loop of ucx_noc_send that waits for the DDMA to become idle (1: the DDMA finished the previous packet of the PE before the send); name_len = bytes of the name of a task (char name[5] of struct tcb_s).

ucx_sleep._doc: kernel/ucx.c: while (cycles--); the header runs cycles + 1 times (the path with cycles < 0 prints and halts)

krnl_delay_update._doc: kernel/sched.c: one pass over the circular list of TCBs

krnl_schedule._doc: kernel/sched.c: search of the next ready task, at most one pass over the circular list

enable_receiver._doc: lib/noc.c: search of the TCB of the receiver in the circular list

ucx_noc_send._doc: lib/noc.c: wait for the idle DDMA (_ddma_send_status); enable_receiver inlined (local packet)

irq4_handler._doc: kernel/sched.c (handler of application E): search of the TCB of task A

ucx_strcmp._doc: lib/libc.c: at most the length of the name plus the terminator

ucx_malloc._doc: lib/malloc.c: first fit; the three loops advance over the list of blocks, at most heap_blocks steps and one exit test per pass of the outer loop in each call

irq_handler._doc: arch/riscv/hf-riscv-e/interrupt.c: one pass per bit of the 8-bit cause (int_control.vhd, irq_cause); the query of each interrupt sets the target of irq_vector[i]()

irq0_handler._doc: interrupt.c: the tick path (TIMER1 CTC): the switch on S0CAUSE & k takes case 0 or case MASK_S0CAUSE_TIMER (4), the latter once (k = 4); timer_vector[i]() calls timer1ctc_handler (hal.c) once; the loop over the bits of the timer cause shifts a 32-bit word right by one per pass (at most 33 tests; the spill and reload of the word around the call hide the shift loop from the analysis); the loop over k is a counted loop (32)

__udivsi3._doc: arch/common/muldiv.c (__udivmodsi4): the loop that shifts the divisor left until bit 31 is set runs at most 32 times; the loop over qbit is a shift loop

_isr._doc: arch/riscv/hf-riscv-e/crt0.s: jalr zero, 0(a5) returns to the interrupted code (address of IRQ_EPC)
